default_answers.alibi: Clinic from before five. I checked on Elias at five past five, as I always do. Returned to the clinic. Heard Owen shout at six.
default_answers.timeline: My routine, as every afternoon. Nothing unusual.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: At five past five. He was fine. He seemed — pleased about something.
default_answers.relationship: I've looked after Elias for six years. This is devastating.
default_answers.location: The clinic, the square, back to the clinic. That's all.

rules.answer_text: We met shortly after I moved to the village and started at the clinic. They brought over a tin of biscuits as a welcome gift. We've been neighbors and friends ever since, sharing quiet moments when the village got too loud.
Elias was my patient for six years. I administered his medication, monitored his heart, sat with him through two scares. I cared for him. People can care for someone and still find them difficult.
suggested_followups: How did you two first meet?

rules.answer_text: I opened the clinic at ten to five. I prepared the afternoon medications — routine. At five past five I walked over to give Elias his pill organiser, as I do every Tuesday when he can't collect it himself. He was well. Cheerful, actually. I went back to the clinic. At six I heard Owen.

claims.summary: Nadia describes her afternoon as entirely routine, including the pill handoff at 17:05.

suggested_followups: What exactly did you give him this afternoon?

rules.answer_text: Those capsules — I cannot explain that. Someone must have interfered with the organiser between when I prepared it and when I gave it to him. Ben was in and out with a clinic pouch before opening, wasn't he? This building is not Fort Knox.

claims.summary: Nadia claims the extra capsules could have been added by someone else after she prepared the organiser.

rules.answer_text: I made an error in the log and corrected it. That is standard procedure. A different ink means I ran out of blue and used what was to hand. There is nothing sinister in a correction.

claims.summary: Nadia says the altered log entry is an ordinary correction, not evidence of falsification.

rules.answer_text: ...Those are private notes. That notebook is locked. How did you —

claims.summary: Nadia is caught off-guard by the budget notes and does not immediately deny their significance.

rules.answer_text: He told me on Monday he was reconsidering. I told him it was his decision. I was... hurt. Of course I was. Two years of planning. But I accepted it. I would not —

claims.summary: Nadia admits Elias told her about the will change but claims she had accepted it.

default_answers.alibi: My round. I always start at five sharp.
default_answers.timeline: I can give you every house and the time I reached it.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Elias? At five exactly. He waved at me. He was fine.
default_answers.relationship: Just the postwoman. We say good afternoon most days.
default_answers.evidence: I keep my eyes open on a round.
default_answers.location: The square bench is one of my landmarks.

rules.answer_text: At five exactly I passed Elias — he waved his flask, same as always. Then at five past, Nadia came out of the clinic and went to him. She gave him something — small, like a little box — and he took some pills with his tea. I watched for a moment because it was sweet, really, her caring for him like that. Then I moved on.

claims.summary: Ruth confirms Elias was healthy at 17:00 and that Nadia gave him pills from a small box at 17:05.

suggested_followups: Did you see what was in the box?

default_answers.alibi: On my round. Square, side streets, back. Same route every day.
default_answers.timeline: I go through the square twice usually.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: I waved at Elias about quarter past, maybe.
default_answers.relationship: Good bloke. Bit opinionated. Always on that bench.

rules.answer_text: I went through the square at about quarter past. Elias was still on the bench but he looked — odd. Hand on his chest, slumped forward slightly. I thought it was the evening chill getting to him — he's always complaining about drafts. I didn't stop. I wish I had.

claims.summary: Ben noticed Elias with his hand on his chest at 17:15 but did not stop.

suggested_followups: Had he seemed well earlier in the afternoon?

rules.answer_text: The complaint letter. Right. Elias caught me signing for parcels I hadn't put straight into people's hands. Stupid, not criminal. The clinic pouch was sealed and I dropped it at reception before Nadia opened. Check the manifest. Check the shops after that. I did not touch his medication.

default_answers.alibi: Yard in the afternoon. I always stop to see Elias at six.
default_answers.timeline: Yard, then square at six. I'm the one who found him.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Yesterday evening. We had a pint. He seemed happy enough.

rules.answer_text: We first met over a job. The roof was leaking and I came to patch it. We shook hands on a fair price, and that was the start of a long working relationship. It's a shame how things turned out.
He was the nosiest man in the village and never wrong when it mattered. I'll miss him.
suggested_followups: How did you two first meet?

rules.answer_text: Yesterday evening at the pub. He said he'd sorted some family business, something about a nephew. Seemed lighter than he'd been in a while. I thought it was good, whatever it was. I didn't think it would be the last time I'd talk to him.

claims.summary: Owen last saw Elias at the pub the previous evening. Elias mentioned 'sorting family business' and seemed relieved.

default_answers.last_seen_victim: From the window at half five or so.
default_answers.evidence: I can tell you what I saw from the cafe window.
default_answers.location: The bench is visible from the till.

rules.answer_text: Half five, maybe a bit before. He was on his bench, slumped to one side. I thought he was asleep — he does that sometimes in the warm months. I should have gone to check. I keep thinking I should have gone to check.

Before Nadia opened, Ben stopped at Elias's bench. It was not friendly. Elias had a folded letter in his hand and Ben looked as if he wanted to snatch it. A few minutes later Ben slipped into the clinic doorway with a pouch and came straight back out. I should have mentioned it, but Ben's a friend and Elias could be... severe.

claims.summary: Clara saw Ben argue with Elias at 16:44 and briefly enter the clinic frontage at 16:48.

suggested_followups: How long was Ben inside the clinic?

default_answers.last_seen_victim: Monday, for his usual check. His heart was irregular but stable.
default_answers.relationship: Patient of twelve years. His condition required careful management.
default_answers.evidence: Show me what you have and I'll tell you what it means.

rules.answer_text: The dispensing log is one book. The cabinet is another — and that one I cannot amend, and neither can she, because every opening is signed and timed against the key. If you want to know what actually left that cabinet on Tuesday, fetch me the cabinet book. ...I would rather you fetched it than I did.

Two 0.25mg capsules? His prescription is 0.125mg once daily. Two of those would be four times his therapeutic dose. Given his arrhythmia, reduced renal function, and the fact he took them with hot tea on an empty stomach... yes, that could kill him unusually fast. A collapse inside twenty minutes is medically credible.

claims.summary: Dr. Haig confirms two 0.25mg digoxin capsules could cause Elias to collapse within twenty minutes and would be fatal without immediate intervention.

rules.answer_text: I sign off Nadia's dispensing records weekly. I trusted her completely — she is meticulous. If you're telling me this entry has been altered... show me. I want to see it myself.

You have found the accounts, then. Yes. The practice does not stand up without that legacy, and I am a partner, not an employee, and I knew the bequest existed because I countersigned the letter.

I am aware of the shape of what you are holding. I would ask you to hold it a little longer before you decide what it is.

claims.summary: Haig admits the practice depends on the Grant legacy and that he knew about the bequest.

rules.answer_text:
Tuesday afternoon I was at the county surgery, which is forty minutes from here on a good road. I saw eleven patients between two and half past six. Every one of them is timed and initialled in my hand, and every one of them was looking at me while I did it.

I attend this clinic at seven, twice a week. I was not in the village when Elias Grant died, and I have spent every hour since wishing I had been.
